== Missing data ==
* No Decipher internal 2nd Edition design document, card list, or mock-up faces survive in public sources. The July 2000 presentation excerpts are the printed pitch. Colson (2022) is the oral-history account of what a later reboot would have looked like.
* LOTR TCG card back is now [[File:LOTR-card-back.jpg]] from Wikipedia File:The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game cardback.jpg (Wayback file page 20251224153727; image 20251119170146).
* archive.org item [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o] exists (BoardMatt, 24 April 2022) but was still processing at dest time. Watch-page Wayback 20261015174310 is the Preserved copy in the refs.
* No other interview (Braunlich Booster Pack #28, Holland TFN license-end, Kallenbach TFN Flashback) names a SWCCG 2nd Edition product beyond the July 2000 pitch. The Kallenbach .hack mixed-deck quote is now in the body, cited from the Dothack Network capture. The Reddit copy (20210701195848) is a login wall with no interview text.

== Possibly faulty data ==
* Colson said WARS had "three major factions, maybe five in total." The printed game has five named factions plus Independent. Body reports both: printed five + Independent, and Colson's count.
* Whisper of the Colson clip heard "reboot, .0"; auto-captions and the wiki transcript give "reboot 2.0". Body uses 2.0. Quotes were checked against the audio (faster-whisper base.en, clips 11:20–15:40 and 1:06:50–1:12:10), not raw captions.
* The July 2000 pitch is backward-compatible 2nd Edition. Colson's later "one back, reboot 2.0" is a different, more complete reboot. Body keeps them in separate sections so the pitch is not rewritten as Colson's reboot.

== Marginal cuts ==
* Howard Roffman (TheForce.Net) said Wizards won the license with "a multi-layered experience within a single game (as opposed to multiple games for different audiences)." Inference that 2E would have unified SWCCG, Young Jedi and Jedi Knights is unsourced. Cut.
* Players Committee ''Beginner's Rulebook'' PDFs titled "2nd Edition" (2021 fan beginner docs) are unrelated. No hatnote.
* Full marketing-program list from the same presentation already lives on [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]]. Not repeated here.
* WARS stack/interrupt, encampments, NōBots, casualty/damage/defense vocabulary: already on [[WARS TCG]]. Only the common back, factions, 4-copy cap and 60-card starters are in the article.
* LOTR ''Shadows'' (2004) partial reboot: already on [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]]. Cut here.

== Build notes ==
* Presentation excerpts: Wayback 20020602000629 of decipher.com/starwars/presentationexcerpts.html, posted by Warren Holland 28 December 2001.
* Colson quotes: yt-dlp section clips, ffmpeg PCM into faster-whisper base.en int8. Auto-captions used for names/titles after Whisper confirmed meaning. Cite &t= seconds.
* WARS 4-copy: Incursion rulebook, "You may include no more than four copies of a single card." Preserved copy 20261008234817.
* Kallenbach mixed-deck quote: Wayback 20251205002711 of dothack.org topic 1346 (opened; full interview text).
* LOTR mixed deck: CR 4.2 Draw Deck, "at least 60 cards and must have an equal number of Shadow cards and Free Peoples cards, shuffled together."
* 16 October 2026: removed the Complexity and Defensive Shields section (Bill: shields are another topic). That narrative is now [[Silver bullets]]. Colson's 2E quotes stay here.
